name: Lorazepam
summary: An intermediate-acting benzodiazepine metabolized by glucuronidation only — the preferred BZD in hepatic impairment and a first-line IV agent for status epilepticus.
mechanism: Positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors, enhancing inhibitory GABAergic transmission.

pharmacokinetics.bioavailability: Well absorbed orally; reliable IM absorption

dosing.adult: 1–2 mg two to three times daily (usual 2–6 mg/day); 2–4 mg IV for status epilepticus

safety.pregnancy: Avoid if possible; floppy infant syndrome with late-pregnancy use.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; infant sedation possible.
contraindications: Severe respiratory insufficiency or sleep apnea
warnings: Boxed warning: dependence, abuse, and withdrawal with long-term use
Boxed warning: respiratory depression when combined with opioids
Respiratory depression risk with IV administration
Falls and cognitive impairment in the elderly
safety.overdose: Sedation and respiratory depression (especially IV or with opioids); flumazenil reversal.

clinicalPearls: No CYP metabolism — the preferred benzodiazepine in hepatic impairment and the elderly.
Reliable IM absorption and a first-line IV status-epilepticus agent (with diazepam).
good: Anxiety in liver disease or the elderly; IV status epilepticus and procedural sedation.
bad: Patients needing sustained around-the-clock anxiolysis (short duration), or long-term BZD therapy.
